turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

Hale. I have a call at 4:40, so we have about twenty minutes. Owen found out about his zero from his phone in the middle of a class, nobody called me first, so start with who decided that and on what basis.
Thanks for coming in, Ms. Kalinowski.
That's not an answer. Who entered the zero, and did anyone speak to Owen before it went in?
The school's AI checker flagged Owen's essay at 94 percent.

A machine's guess, Hale, and the company that sells it says in its own guide not to use it as the sole basis for punishing a student. Your school's procedure 4.3 says the same thing, and I have both printed in my bag. So what else do you have, or is that it?
That's very high. The software is quite reliable.

"Quite reliable." Stanford tested seven of these detectors and they flagged sixty-one percent of essays by non-native English writers as machine-written, so I'm writing down that your whole case is a percentage. If that's all there is, I'm going to the principal's office when we're done.
So I had to give him a zero.

"Had to." Your own procedure says you speak with the student first and call the parent before any mark is entered, and you did neither. I'm writing down that the zero came first, and I want it off today.
I hope you understand my position.
Don't manage me, Hale. Your position is a number from a machine and a zero entered before anyone called me. Withdraw it, or show me something with a date on it.
